quest.title: Yae Publishing House's Invitation
quest.description: Aratani, an editor at the Yae Publishing House, seems to have something she'd like a little help with...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Ugh, how am I supposed to contact these two authors in this situation...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Contact who now?

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Oh! Traveler, it's you... Thank goodness you're here. I was just in need of someone's help!

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Here's the problem: Yae Publishing House's annual novel-writing competition is about to begin, and as is our rule, we plan to invite a few of our writers to serve on the judging panel.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: However, we have two writers who are neither Inazuman, nor do they currently reside in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: As you know, the present circumstances prevent us from inviting outlanders here.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: But if we fail to inform the writers of such an important matter, that would also be inappropriate...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: So I thought that if someone could at least send them a gift, the basic courtesies would at least be satisfied. And we could also attach a letter discussing future manuscripts— *cough* I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Would you be willing to help me out?

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: Chang the Ninth's story, known as the "First Apprentice of Guhua," is a tale about the first apprentice of a famed martial arts school in Liyue and a young girl from Inazuma whom he took on as a junior apprentice.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: If you were to ask me, the themes and plot are just a little outdated by this point, but enough readers buy it to keep sales up.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: We often ask people to send some letters to him to suggest certain changes he might make in future works to perhaps make a breakthrough...

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: But we have never received a reply. Perhaps the letters were lost on the way, or...

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: Now this one, I have no idea about. It's likely a pen name of some sort.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: But the book "A Legend of Sword"? That one's an earth-shatterer and a world-shaker, make no mistake!

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: Both the setting and the story have sent veritable shocks throughout the literary world!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, where do I find this writer, then...

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: Hmm. I believe that this writer also lives in Liyue. According to a traveling merchant who brought this book back to Inazuma, he first found this text at Wanwen Bookhouse.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: I think that if you ask the staff at Wanwen Bookhouse, you should be able to find this author.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: However... *cough* Well, never mind that for now. Here are the presents and the letters. I'm putting this in your reliable hands, Traveler!

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: One of them is named Zhenyu, and the other is... Chang the Ninth.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Hmm? Traveler? What brings you to my home today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here's a letter and a gift from Yae Publishing House.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: A letter from Yae Publishing House? They're not asking me to change my pen name again, are they?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I've told them a thousand times that I'll write under my real name...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: *sigh* Oh, forget it. Let me have a look...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: They want me to judge a novel-writing contest... Hmm. I don't think I have the time, but I suppose I should thank them, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Eh? What's all this? These are... "creative suggestions"...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Uh, I—I'll have to read these a bit more carefully. Thank you, Traveler.

talks.objective: Search for Zhenyu at the Wanwen Bookhouse

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Hmm, this part is indeed well-written, and the progression is so very novel...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Xingqiu.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's what happens. Fascinating...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Xingqiu!

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: #Hmm? Ah, it's you, {NICKNAME}. It has been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: From the way you greeted me, you seem well. That is good... What brings you here today?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, we were hoping to ask you to find someone for us. You've read a ton of books, so you probably know.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: A person? Are you looking for a writer, then? Hmm... certainly, ask away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're looking for a certain "Zhenyu"...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Zhenyu? Wh—Where did you hear this name?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It says so right here on this copy of "A Legend of Sword"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're looking for this Zhenyu person because someone from Yae Publishing House in Inazuma asked us to pass them a letter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Would you know who this Zhenyu person is?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Well, this Zhenyu of whom you speak...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: This is embarrassing, but... that's my pen name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, that's one we've never heard of.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Well, it's certainly nothing worth mentioning.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Initially, the editor in charge of this book here in Liyue told me that "the setting is too outlandish while the plot is unexpectedly clichéd. No one will like this," and rejected my manuscript.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I didn't feel like taking that lying down, so I had a few copies printed myself before planting them surreptitiously into Wanwen Bookhouse to see if anyone would like them.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: As it turned out, readers were few and far between, so I did not pay it any more mind. I never thought that it would become so popular in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Still, I'm quite pleased that people are willing to read what I've written.

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: I shall read this letter carefully, Traveler. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back at last! How did it go? Did you find our two authors?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I did. The letters have been delivered.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: That's wonderful! What did they say, Traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They both said that they'd read the letters with care.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Good, good. *sigh* It's just a shame that they're both far away in Liyue. Even were things more normal, we couldn't easily go to visit them.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Especially for Mr. Zhenyu. His book, "A Legend of Sword," wasn't even submitted by him, but by a traveling merchant.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Later, one of our editors would read this book, and seeing its value, they prepared to go to Liyue personally and arrange for more manuscripts to be written.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Who would've thought that with these changes in our situation, none of our letters that we sought to have people bring to Liyue ever returned.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: We could only publish the books first, while keeping a record of the royalties owed to Mr. Zhenyu. Once we'd established contact, we would send the royalties over.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: But it's been so long, and still "A Legend of Sword" remains a bestseller. The royalties are starting to pile up...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: *sigh* How I wish Mr. Zhenyu could attend this competition. These royalties can't be left to pile up like this much longer...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back at last! How did it go? Did you find our two authors?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I did. The letters have been delivered.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: That's wonderful! What did they say, Traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They both said that they'd read the letters with care.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Good, good. *sigh* It's just a shame that they're both far away in Liyue. Even we couldn't easily go to visit them any day we like.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: This is especially the case for Mr. Zhenyu. His book, "A Legend of Sword," wasn't even submitted by him, but by a traveling merchant.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Later, one of our editors would read this book, and seeing its value, they prepared to go to Liyue personally and arrange for more manuscripts to be written.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: But who would've thought... The situation here kept changing, one of our plans kept getting delayed, and none of the letters we had sent ever returned.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: We could only publish the books first, while keeping a record of the royalties owed to Mr. Zhenyu. Once we'd established contact, we would send the royalties over.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: *sigh* How I wish Mr. Zhenyu could attend this competition. These royalties can't be left to pile up like this much longer...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: *sigh* When will we be able to see Mr. Zhenyu's next work?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: How are there this many suggestions for future writing subjects...

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Still, I wonder — how did the book that I wrote manage to make it over the ocean to Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Xingqiu
dialogues.text: Did some passing Inazuman merchant buy the book before bringing it home with them?
